messages.subject: How to specify type of cross when using a csv dataset
messages.subject_clean: How to specify type of cross when using a csv dataset
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am just beginning to learn how to use R/QTL and have recently
completed the tutorials with the provided datasets and am now trying
the same analyses with my dataset.  It appears that the default cross
types are either f2 or bc.  I've found references suggesting that R/QTL
can also analyze data from recombinant inbred lines ("riself");
however, I can't seem to find what command to use or where to include
this information so that R knows that this is the appropriate cross.
I'm not sure that it matters, but I'm importing my data as a .csv file.
 Any advice on where to find this information, or how to do this?
Thanks,
Jen

messages.subject: Re: How to specify type of cross when using a csv dataset
messages.subject_clean: How to specify type of cross when using a csv dataset
messages.body_plain:
The analysis of RILs is not yet fully documented, but I do
believe things are working.

Read it in as if it were a backcross, and then switch the
first part of the object's "class" from "bc" to "riself"
if you're looking at recombinant inbred lines by selfing,
or "risib" for RILs obtained by sibling mating.
For example:

   myx <- read.cross("csv", [blah blah blah])
   class(myx)[1] <- "riself"

regards,
karl

messages.subject: Output for multiple QTLs above LOD threshold on 1 chromosome
messages.subject_clean: Output for multiple QTLs above LOD threshold on 1 chromosome
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
The command summary.scanone only reports the maximum LOD score on each
chromsome, but there may be more than one QTL per chromsome.  For
example, there are 2 very large peaks on chromosome 1 when I look at
the data graphically using plot.scanone.  Is there any command to get R
to report these other high LOD values and corresponding marker
locations (i.e. to report multiple regions on a single chromosome that
exceed a specified LOD threshold)?
Thanks,
Jen

p.s. Thanks for your quick reply to my last post, Karl...the "riself"
commands seemed to work fine (I'll double check with another program
too though to make sure).

messages.subject: Re: Output for multiple QTLs above LOD threshold on 1 chromosome
messages.subject_clean: Output for multiple QTLs above LOD threshold on 1 chromosome
messages.body_plain:
There's no easy way to pick off the other peaks.  If you type the
name of the object storing the scanone results (call it "output"),
you'll see all of the results.  Or if you type, for example,

   output[output[,1]=="5",]

you'll see the output for chromosome 5.

Or type

   output[output[,1]=="5" & output[,3]>2,]

you'll see the parts on chromosome 5 that have LOD scores about 2.

karl

messages.subject: R/qtl version 1.01-9
messages.body_plain:
A new version of R/qtl (1.01-9) has been released at its web site
(http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/qtl).

See http://www.biostat.jhsph.edu/~kbroman/qtl/STATUS.txt for a list of
changes.  Users interested in the use of gene expression microarray
data as phenotypes will be pleased to find new data import formats,
similar to the "csv" format, but either rotated ("csvr", exchanging the
columns and rows), allowing different files for genotype and phenotype
data ("csvs"), or both ("csvsr").  I hope this will speed up data
import considerably.

As always, I'd appreciate hearing any suggestions or comments or
complaints.

Karl Broman
